episodes.167884: Numerous marine thunderstorm wind gusts occurred.
episodes.167897: A humid air mass situated over central Indiana, up to a warm front stretched across the region's far-northern counties, provided ample instability;  while adequate levels of vertical wind shear were also present, especially closer to the boundary.  Within this environment, numerous late day, strong thunderstorms moved quickly through the region from south to north.  Early in the evening, scattered wind damage was produced by the two most prominent cells, in Madison County and across several of the region's north-central counties.
episodes.168036: A longwave trough over the center of the country pushed a weak cold front through Deep South Texas and the Rio Grande Valley early in the morning of May 25th. The cold front had a line of showers and thunderstorms associated with it, which strengthened substantially as it moved out of Kenedy and Brooks Counties and into Willacy, Cameron, and Hidalgo Counties. There were several measured wind gusts over 58 mph, with the strongest being recorded at SpaceX on Boca Chica Beach of 72 mph.
episodes.168037: A longwave trough over the center of the country pushed a weak cold front through the Lower Texas Coastal Waters the morning of May 25th. As the cold front pushed south, it strengthened due to more available energy over the region. This lead to several Marine Thunderstorm Wind gusts in excess of 34 knots or 39 mph. The strongest Marine Thunderstorm Wind was 61 knots, or 70 mph, at the SPI Brazos Santiago Station.
episodes.168069: Mostly large branches and some small sheds that were lofted from this weak tornado.  Storm spotters shared video of the tornado from a nearby field.
episodes.168070: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours ahead of a slow moving low pressure system.
episodes.168078: Strong to locally severe storms developed in a modestly unstable atmosphere, aided by a 50 knot mid level wave. A few marginally severe wind gusts were recorded along with some tree damage in a few locations.
episodes.168138: A deepening are of low pressure associated with a storm system centered over eastern Nebraska was in place Wednesday morning on May 25th. A warm sector was in place over much of northern Alabama east of this feature. Two lines of thunderstorms developed in this warm sector. The first line of convection occurred in the morning hours over northeastern Alabama and produced one supercell that was short lived. This supercell storm produced a brief tornado touchdown east of the Painter community.  More strong to severe storms occurred with the second round of convection that affected NW Alabama with damaging winds before weakening as it moved further east during the afternoon hours.
episodes.168280: A series of strong thunderstorms resulted in tree damage during the early morning hours of May 25.
episodes.168448: Scattered thunderstorms moved across northern Illinois during the afternoon of May 25th producing several funnel clouds.
episodes.168449: Scattered severe thunderstorms moved across parts of northwest Indiana on May 25th.
episodes.168450: Scattered severe thunderstorms moved across parts of southern Lake Michigan during the afternoon and evening of May 25th.
episodes.168676: Isolated gale-force wind gusts occurred oceanside of Key West as scattered showers and a few thunderstorms embedded in strong east-southeast lower tropospheric flow passed through the vicinity.
episodes.168738: A brief spin-up tornado occurred Wednesday afternoon just south of Freeport near the airport.  No injuries were reported.
episodes.168771: An upper-level closed low moved east across the lower Mississippi River Valley. Several weak upper-level disturbances embedded in the southwest flow aloft moved across the Mid-South. This resulted in showers and thunderstorms across the with damaging wind and heavy rainfall.
episodes.169358: Multiple rounds of strong to severe storms affected the area with impacts to trees and power lines.  In addition, persistent heavy rain along the coast resulted in flooding in portions of Gulf county with over a foot of rain reported.
episodes.169375: A weak cold front brought a round of strong thunderstorms to the area with a few gusts measured in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.169626: An isolated severe thunderstorm produce winds of 60mph which damaged several trees and knocked down some power lines.
episodes.169697: An upper level trough moved across the southern plains pushing a cold front into South Central Texas. Thunderstorms developed along the front and some of these storms produced large hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.169762: With plenty of instability and large scale support as a shortwave moved through the region, a line of showers and storms developed and moved east through the region. Some of the storms produced damaging winds.
episodes.169763: With plenty of instability and large scale support as a shortwave moved through the region, a line of showers and storms developed and moved east through the region. Some of the storms produced damaging winds.
episodes.169840: A strong storm system moved through the Lower Mississippi Valley on May 25th. An associated line of severe thunderstorms moved across portions of Mississippi producing damaging winds and two tornadoes.
episodes.169847: A strong storm system moved through the Lower Mississippi Valley on May 25th. An associated line of severe thunderstorms moved across portions of northeast Louisiana producing damaging winds.
episodes.169942: A surface outflow boundary and dryline was located across the Concho Valley during the afternoon hours along with strong instability to the south of the boundary. Scattered severe thunderstorms quickly developed across the Concho Valley by late afternoon and the combination of the strong instability and deep layer shear resulted in a few supercells. These storms produced baseball to one report of softball size hail across Irion and Tom Green counties. The severe storms then moved into the Heartland and produced large hail and wind damage through the early evening. A few more severe thunderstorms moved southeast into the Concho Valley from the Permian Basin and produced marginal severe hail and strong wind gusts around 70 mph.
episodes.170046: A strong cold front moving through the region on the 25th. A broken line of thunderstorms developed along the frontal boundary. The strongest storms were on the leading edge of the line and produced severe winds in the coastal waters.
episodes.170047: A strong cold front moving through the region on the 25th. A broken line of thunderstorms developed along the frontal boundary. A few storms developed ahead of the main line of storms for a short period before the main line caught up to them. This resulted in a longer period of rainfall for some areas of New Orleans metro which lead to flash flooding.
episodes.170048: A strong cold front moving through the region on the 25th. A broken line of thunderstorms developed along the frontal boundary. The strongest storms were on the leading edge of the line. One portion of the line began to bow out produced damaging winds in Harrison County.
episodes.170061: An area of low pressure over north-central Missouri with an associated occluded front arcing southeastward into the Ozarks triggered a band of thunderstorms across central Illinois during the evening of May 25th.  Some of the storms produced wind gusts of around 60mph and isolated wind damage across portions of Morgan, Sangamon, and Logan Counties.
episodes.170096: A short wave trough interacted with a warm front lifting northward across north central Alabama.  There was sufficient instability to produce marginally severe hail.
episodes.170113: Thunderstorms developed over the higher terrain in northeast Mexico during the afternoon hours of the 24th as an upper level trough interacted with strong instability along and west of the Rio Grande. The storms moved southeast toward the Rio Grande during the evening hours and reached the Laredo area during the latter part of the evening. The storms produced large hail up to the size of limes on the northwest side of Laredo.
episodes.170135: Storms that developed over the Brush Country and over south-central Texas moved into south Texas during the early morning hours of the 25th. Damaging winds occurred over portions of the Coastal Bend and the Victoria Crossroads. The winds mainly caused damage to trees.
episodes.170151: Thunderstorms over the Victoria Crossroads and Coastal Bend moved into the coastal waters during the early morning hours of the 25th. Storms produced wind gusts from 35 to 45 knots across the coastal waters of the Middle Texas coast during the morning hours.
episodes.170172: A warm front slowly lifted north across the area producing a couple days of thunderstorms. Some became severe.
episodes.170173: A warm front slowly lifted north across the area producing thunderstorms. One storm became severe in Southeast Texas producing a tornado.
episodes.170219: A TUTT low enhanced the diurnally induced afternoon convection across sections of central and western Puerto Rico between May 23-26. This created long-lasting thunderstorms with periods of heavy rainfall that led to flash flooding and mudslides. Also, the thunderstorms produced small hail and wind damage.
episodes.170247: An intense line of storms produced wind damage in and around the Pensacola metro area along with a brief tornado.
episodes.170251: A severe thunderstorm produced strong winds on Dauphin Island.
episodes.170284: On May 21st, thunderstorms developed along a combination of a dryline and cold front across the southwestern portions of the region. These storms merged into an eastward moving complex of storms that produced strong winds across some of our Central Texas counties. On May 24th, numerous showers and storms affected the area due primarily to a series of boundaries and shortwaves. A complex of storms moved across parts of Central Texas but was weakening, and only one report of severe criteria winds was reported.
episodes.170317: Strong thunderstorms moved across the marine area and produced high winds.
episodes.170352: A slow moving trough and a cold front provided lift for numerous shower and thunderstorm development. Instability was fairly low, however, with only a few reports of severe wind received.
episodes.170456: Heavy rain late in May brought flooding to the Ouachita River and Cache River.||Another round of rain and thunderstorms occurred on May 24th, with some locations seeing locally heavy rainfall, especially across portions of western and eastern Arkansas. A few storms were rotating, but there were no reports of tornadoes or much severe weather at all. Cool temperatures followed in the wake of the storms with another round of coolest high temperature records across northern Arkansas on the 24th. Dry conditions and warming temperatures were in place at the end of the month.
episodes.170497: Numerous showers and thunderstorms affected Middle Tennessee on May 25 and again on May 26, mainly during the afternoon hours. Several reports of large hail and wind damage were received.

At 10:28 AM on Wednesday, May 25th 2022, an EF-0 tornado touched down near an open-walled garage and caused minor roof damage to the metal roofing panels. The tornado then tracked north-northwest, crossing CR-34 and directly hitting an open-walled chicken house. While most of the roof was damaged, the open walls allowed for the tornado to more easily loft portions of the roof and cause damage to metal roofing panels, so a lower-end estimate of 70 mph was given. This was the maximum width identifiable in the damage pattern for the weak tornado, as roughly two-thirds of the building had roof damage. The tornado then continued north-northwest, uprooting a few trees before rapidly lifting. Due to waterlogged soils from antecedent heavy rainfall, a low-end wind estimate of 73 mph was provided for the uprooted trees. Overall, the tornado lasted less than a minute as it tracked a quarter-mile from south-southeast to the north-northwest embedded within a QLCS.

The tornado was rated EF1 with maximum winds around 100 mph. The tornado was on the ground for nearly 2 miles. Start and end times were estimated by radar. There were no injuries reported. Assistance from Stephenson County Emergency Management in completing the survey is greatly appreciated.
